reasons: The Frameworks page is not visible in this packet, so the link is unverified.
Highlighting does not work for sub-pages such as a single tool page.

terms.meaning: a web address that leads to a page
the part of the web address after the site name, used to decide which menu item is current
a layout where an element stays in place on screen while the rest of the page scrolls

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Loads the current-address reader, the link helper, the menu icons, the animation library, and the logo component.
sections.why: Needed to know the current page and to draw the menu and logo.

sections.name: navItems
sections.title: Menu entries
sections.what: Lists the four menu items with their address, label, and icon: Index, Console, Tools, and Frameworks.
sections.why: Keeps the menu in one place, so adding a page means adding one entry.
sections.watch_out: The Frameworks entry points to a page that is not in this packet, so confirm that page exists before relying on it.

sections.name: Navigation (part 1)
sections.title: Sidebar, logo, and scroll shading
sections.what: Draws the fixed left sidebar with the logo and the goku.ai name. Once the page is scrolled past about 40 pixels, the background becomes darker and a shadow appears.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the sidebar readable over content as the visitor scrolls.
sections.watch_out: The sidebar is fixed at a set width on the left, so page content needs matching left spacing or it will sit underneath.

sections.name: Navigation (part 2)
sections.title: Menu buttons and version label
sections.what: Draws each menu item as a button and highlights the one matching the current address. Shows the typed version label at the bottom.
sections.why: Shows the visitor where they are. The version label is a fixed piece of text with no logic.
sections.watch_out: Highlighting uses an exact match, so a single tool page does not highlight the Tools item.

summary: The fixed left sidebar with the site name, logo, and four main page links, plus a version label at the bottom.
purpose: Lets a visitor move between the main sections of the site and shows which section they are in.
why: Reason for keeping the sidebar fixed not stated in the code. A fixed menu stays reachable while the page scrolls.
how: Reads the current web address and listens for scrolling. Draws the logo and site name, then each menu link, highlighting the one that matches the current address. Shows the version label last.
inputs: The current web address, the scroll position, and the menu list defined in this file.
outputs: A sidebar on screen. Clicking a link moves the visitor to that page.
risks: Highlighting uses an exact address match, so sub-pages do not highlight their parent item. The Frameworks link points to a page that is not in this packet, so it may be broken. The version label is typed text that must be edited by hand.
debug: If the wrong menu item is highlighted, check the address in the menu list and the current address. If the sidebar shading does not change on scroll, check the scroll listener. If page content hides under the sidebar, check the left spacing of the page.
